goal: Review follow-up: a directory record covers the directory path itself, and the red gate counts only AssertionError failures as assertions

built.summary: Changed only worker.py: directory records cover their own path, and non-AssertionError failures count as errors. All five requested checks passed.
non-claims: Record-path and red-gate checks emitted ResourceWarnings from unchanged file-reading code.

e-review-tests: The brief says 'every earlier test in both files must still pass (35 in test_record_paths.py, 72 in test_red_gate.py)', but the existing test_G7_previous_slices_tests_unchanged_and_passing asserts `git diff --quiet HEAD -- test_record_paths.py`. Adding the R8 class, which the brief requires, fails it with 'test_record_paths.py changed'. 71 of the 72 earlier test_red_gate.py tests pass. G7 also runs test_record_paths.py, so it stays red until these files are committed and the R8 build lands. I left G7 unchanged.

'fail closed for any failure type that cannot be established as an AssertionError': no real unittest file can produce a failure whose type is unknown to the harness. This is covered only through custom and non-AssertionError failureException types (Exception, BaseException, RuntimeError, an ad-hoc Exception subclass). A REPORT failure carrying no exception info at all is not tested.

The R8 rule 'for every consumer (tree_state, both inventories)' is tested for the directory's own path through is_record, tree_state and the no-tree-changes validator only. worker.inventory reads .py files, so a bare directory path never reaches it as an entry; the inventories are not separately tested for the directory-itself case.

R8 'no filesystem stat or type check turns it into a directory' is tested with the process cwd set to a repo holding a directory 'mangsang', and through tree_state with a lock declaring the bare 'mangsang'. No test can rule out a stat against some other base path.
